newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Investor looks at joint Finn bank - paper.
newsitem.headline: Investor looks at joint Finn bank - paper.

text.p: Swedish investment company Investor AB, controlled by the Wallenberg industrial dynasty, and Finland's finance family Ehrnrooth are planning to set up a new bank in Finland, a Swedish newspaper reported on Thursday.
Business daily Dagens Industri said Ane Gyllenberg Private Bank of Finland, controlled by the two prominent financial families, has applied for a permit to start a new bank.
"This isn't anything dramatic. It is part of our property management concept," Andreas Stenius, who is set to become president of the new bank, told Dagens Industri.
The new Arne Gyllenberg subsidiary, which will have starting capital of 60 million crowns, intends to target short-term placements, the paper said.

Ane Gyllenberg is 31.5 percent owned by Investor and 31.5 percent owned by the Ehrnrooth family's Agrofin. It administers about 12 billion crowns for its clients, making it the market leader in Finland.
